concept.title: People with long-term health conditions
concept.shortdesc: People living with a chronic, progressive, painful or life-limiting physical illness or injury, or recovering from one, and their families.

conbody.note: Draft group. Groups are a convenience for browsing the draft: the hierarchy was proposed by a second clustering pass and named by a language model, and no person has reviewed it.

ul.li: : People who have had a stroke, TIA or acquired brain injury, including those with related communication difficulties such as aphasia, and those close to them.
: People living with arthritis, painful or stiff joints and similar musculoskeletal complaints.
: People living with fibromyalgia, ME/CFS or other persistent pain and fatigue conditions.
: People living with multiple sclerosis (MS), and their carers, sometimes alongside other progressive or fatiguing conditions.
: People living with Parkinson's disease or related progressive neurological conditions such as motor neurone disease and Huntington's, and their families.
: People regaining strength or movement after an injury, operation or illness.
: People with an incurable or advanced illness who need palliative or hospice care, and their families.
: People diagnosed with cancer, living beyond it, or bereaved by it, and their families.
: People living with any ongoing or chronic medical condition, described in general terms rather than by a named illness.
